title: Targeting tankyrase scaffolding in the β-catenin destruction complex by PROTAC overcomes the limitation of catalytic inhibitors in colorectal cancer
abstract: Aberrant WNT/β-catenin signaling drives tumorigenesis and metastasis in cancer. Although enzymatic inhibitors of tankyrase (TNKS) effectively block AXIN degradation and stabilize the β-catenin destruction complex (DC), they have demonstrated limited efficacy in various colorectal cancer (CRC) models. Here, we demonstrate that, unexpectedly, the induction of AXIN puncta represents a major barrier to achieving therapeutic efficacy. Mechanistically, catalytic inhibition of TNKS prevents TNKS turnover and drives its accumulation in the DC, wherein the scaffolding function of TNKS induces AXIN puncta formation, rigidifies the DC, and impedes β-catenin turnover. Chemically induced degradation of TNKS overcomes this limitation by stabilizing AXIN without puncta formation, providing a deeper suppression of the WNT/β-catenin pathway activity and the proliferation of CRC cells harboring dysfunctional APC mutations. title: A novel mechanism for morphological change during bacterial sporulation based on programmed peptidoglycan degradation
abstract: Many bacteria form spores to endure unfavorable conditions. While Firmicutes generate endospores through cell division, sporulation in non-Firmicutes remains less understood. The Gram-negative bacterium Myxococcus xanthus undergoes sporulation through two distinct mechanisms: rapid sporulation triggered by chemical induction and slow sporulation driven by starvation, both occurring independently of cell division. Instead, these processes depend on the complete degradation of the peptidoglycan (PG) cell wall by two lytic transglycosylases (LTGs), LtgA and LtgB. Remarkably, LtgB programs the pace of PG degradation by LtgA during rapid sporulation, ensuring a controlled process that prevents abrupt PG breakdown and the formation of non-resistant pseudospores. In addition to regulation between LTGs, PG degradation is also influenced by its synthesis; cells exhibiting increased muropeptide production often circumvent sporulation. title: Antibiotic stewardship challenges in Madagascar’s poultry sector: informality, knowledge gaps, and market constraints
abstract:
by Sophie Molia, Ilo Tsimok’Haja Ramahatafandry, Michel Rakotoharinome, Christian Lienhardt, Muriel Figuié, Alexandre Hobeika, Daouda Kassié

Antibiotic resistance (ABR) is a major global public health threat, largely driven by the overuse and misuse of antibiotics. Tackling its animal health component is particularly difficult in low- and middle-income countries, where data and resources are limited. This qualitative study aims to explore antibiotic use (ABU) and its underlying drivers in poultry farms in Analamanga, Madagascar’s region with the highest poultry density. In April 2023, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 79 poultry farmers (13 backyard and 66 semi-intensive), 10 animal health professionals, and 10 agrovet shop sellers. title: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11212-0

A high-throughput CRISPR-interference platform allows the mapping of interactions between essential genes in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, revealing many previously unknown genetic interactions and providing insight into gene function and drug–target relationships that could enable the development of new therapies for tuberculosis.

title: A national baseline for methane sink habitats and methanotroph diversity
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79316-9

In this study, the authors use metagenomics to map the diverse and previously unknown bacteria responsible for taking up methane across Denmark’s varied environments and highlight the natural habitats and methanotroph species with the potential for methane mitigation.

title: Harrowing experiences of vagina fistula victims in the Kpandai District of Ghana: A qualitative study
abstract:
by Eric Elorm Ahorsu, Joshua Adeti, Ernest Kemevor Selasie, Mohammed Ibn Shamsudeen, Cynthia Akos Okumasi, Benjamin Amedume, Justice Wiston Amstrong Jonathan

Background

Vaginal fistula (VF), particularly vesicovaginal fistula (VVF), remains a significant reproductive health challenge in many low-resource settings, including the Kpandai District of Ghana. Despite its profound physical and psychosocial impact, the lived experiences of affected women in rural districts remain under-documented.

Aim

This study explored the lived experiences of women diagnosed with vesicovaginal fistula in the Kpandai District of Ghana, focusing on their physical, emotional, and social challenges, as well as coping strategies.

title: Epidemiological surveillance of bacterial pathogens in cultured European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) along the Aegean coast of Türkiye
abstract:
by Pınar Çelik, Vyron Georgalas, İhsan Çelik

Intensive aquaculture of European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) along the Aegean coast of Türkiye faces continuous production challenges from infectious diseases, yet comprehensive multi-year baseline data remain limited. This study presents a multi-year retrospective surveillance program (2020–2025) monitoring bacterial pathogens associated with 748 distinct cage-level disease outbreaks in fish across 19 discrete offshore commercial sea farms. To maintain industry confidentiality, diagnostic data from these separate facilities were fully aggregated and evaluated across three broad macro-regional surveillance zones. A total of 5,235 fish displaying clinical signs underwent diagnostic necropsy. Presumptive bacterial identification was conducted using phenotypic profiling through the API 20E system, and organ touch-imprint cytology. title: Midbrain somatostatin-expressing cells control pain-suppression during defensive states
abstract: In threatening situations, animals exhibit a broad range of behavioral and autonomic responses. As such, a crucial adaptive response is the inhibition of pain, which facilitates relevant defensive behaviors that promote survival. Whereas the structures and mechanisms involved in fear and pain behaviors are well documented, little is known about the precise neuronal mechanisms mediating the emotional regulation of endogenous pain-suppression. Here, we used a combination of behavioral, anatomical, optogenetic, and electrophysiological approaches to investigate, in male mice, the role of somatostatin-expressing cells in the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray matter (SST<sup>+</sup> vlPAG cells) in the control of analgesia induced during defensive states. Our data indicate that optogenetic inhibition of SST<sup>+</sup> vlPAG cells promotes analgesia irrespective of animal defensive state. title: Virus-specific impacts on honey bee flight performance are mediated by the octopamine pathway
abstract: High annual honey bee colony losses are associated with environmental and biological stressors, including virus infections. In insects, the octopamine (OA) pathway orchestrates the ‘fight-or-flight’ response, regulating energy mobilization, temperature, and flight. We determined that sacbrood virus (SBV) infections induce expression of an OA receptor and enhance honey flight performance, whereas deformed wing virus (DWV) infections reduce flight performance, but how viruses interface with this pathway remained unknown. To elucidate the relationships between the OA response, virus infection, and flight, honey bees were infected with SBV or DWV and exposed to OA, epinastine (EP) – an OA receptor antagonist, or both OA and EP; flight and gene expression were assessed. Pharmacologic manipulation revealed that OA supplementation rescued flight deficits in DWV-infected bees, but diminished performance in SBV-infected bees, while blocking OA receptors altered these effects. title: Sperm phospholipase C signaling via PLCζ1 and PLCδ4 is essential for Ca<sup>2+</sup> oscillations and fertility in mice
abstract:
by Neha Gupta, Lei Zhang, Hiroki Akizawa, Maria G. Gervasi, Darya A. Tourzani, Pablo E. Visconti, Ana Romarowski, Mariano Buffone, Wei Cui, Rafael A. Fissore

Fertilization-induced calcium (Ca2+) oscillations are essential for egg activation and embryonic development in mammals. The sperm-specific phospholipase C isoform, PLCζ1, is the primary trigger of these oscillations. Functional and clinical studies have linked mutations or reduced expression of PLCζ1 to male infertility. However, whether PLCζ1 alone accounts for Ca2+ release at fertilization in all mammals remains uncertain. Male mice lacking Plcζ1 exhibit subfertility and reduced litter sizes; their sperm induce delayed, low-frequency Ca2+ oscillations, indicating a compensatory mechanism. title: A split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers define the tail architecture of Pseudomonas aeruginosa podophage A1002
abstract:
by Hao Pang, Yuan Chen, Zeng Peng, Hao Xiao, Wenyuan Chen, Xiaowu Li, Ping Chen, Jing Zheng, Hongrong Liu

Phage therapy offers unique advantages against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. However, high-resolution structural studies of phages targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa—a top-seven global pathogen—particularly podophages, remain severely limited, directly impeding structure-based development of novel antimicrobials. In this study, we utilize cryo-EM to resolve the high-resolution intact structure of mature phage A1002, a podophage infecting carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa. Based on density maps combined with AlphaFold3 predictions, we identified 11 structural protein components from the head to the tail. Phage A1002 exhibits a distinctly elongated tail morphology distinct from other reported podophages. title: A deep genetic structure phylogenomically frames the closest algal relatives of land plants
abstract:
by Maaike J. Bierenbroodspot, Cäcilia F. Kunz, Elisa S. Goldbecker, Maike Lorenz, Iker Irisarri, Thomas Pröschold, Tatyana Darienko, Jan de Vries

Discerning the nature of the last common ancestor of land plants (embryophytes) and algae allows to retrace the adaptations that ushered in the conquest of land by plants. For this, the closest streptophyte algal relatives of embryophytes hold key information. Albeit initially coming as a surprise due to their plain body plans, all major phylogenomic efforts have concluded that the Zygnematophyceae are the algal sisters to land plants. The Zygnematophyceae are the streptophyte algal class with the greatest species richness and while we now have ample genome information on a few select members of zygnematophytes, our understanding of the genomic divergence as well as genetic potential for key traits is limited by a lack of phylodiverse data that accounts for this diversity and integrates it into a phylogenomic framework. title: Infant presence and mother-infant conflict predict fetal loss in wild mandrills
abstract:
by Nikolaos Smit, Berta Roura-Torres, Axelle Delaunay, Alice Baniel, Elise Huchard, Marie J. E. Charpentier

Female fitness depends on reproductive pace and offspring survival, both of which are determined by the ability to balance resource allocation between current and future reproduction. Using 11 years of data on 356 pregnancies (52 of which resulted in fetal loss) from 117 wild female mandrills, we show that females who conceive while still caring for a young infant experience a greater probability of fetal loss as well as increased mother-infant behavioral conflict in the form of maternal rejection. In addition, females whose infants throw more tantrums show a greater probability of fetal loss, consistent with observations from other species where living offspring can interfere in parental reproduction. Background

title: Transforming pandemic influenza antiviral stockpiling using a capacity-based approach: A modeling study
abstract:
by Nir Gavish, Amit Huppert

Background

Pandemic influenza preparedness in high-resource nations has traditionally relied on large antiviral stockpiles, typically targeting coverage for 25% of the population. This inventory-based benchmark focuses on cumulative disease burden but often overlooks the inelastic capacity of healthcare systems to manage acute surges. As multi-billion-dollar inventories reach expiration, we evaluated whether static stockpiles remain a viable strategy for preventing healthcare system collapse during future pandemics.

Methods and findings

We projected daily hospital bed demand using three complementary frameworks: a static lower-bound estimation, a dynamic deterministic Susceptible-Infectious-Hospitalized-Recovered transmission model, and historical reconstructions of the 1918, 1957, and 1968 pandemics using mortality data. title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation on vitamin D status and physical performance in football players: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract:
by Jinfa Gu, Yu Zhang, Luhua Xiao

Background/Objectives

Low vitamin D status is frequently reported among athletes, but whether vitamin D supplementation improves physical performance in football players remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of vitamin D supplementation on serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] concentration, jump performance, sprint performance, aerobic capacity, and muscular performance in association football and futsal players.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to 31 May 2026. Controlled intervention studies comparing vitamin D supplementation with control conditions were eligible. Standardized mean differences were calculated as Hedges’ g and pooled using random-effects meta-analyses. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using RoB 2 or ROBINS-I. title: Global return-on-investment of COVID-19 vaccines in the first year of the vaccination programme: A model-based economic evaluation
abstract:
by Hallie Benjamin, Gregory Barnsley, Oliver J. Watson, Mark Jit

Background

COVID-19 vaccines played a critical role in reducing global health burden during the COVID-19 pandemic, but their rapid development required extraordinary effort. This study aims to evaluate their global return-on-investment (ROI) during the first year of the vaccination programme (8 December 2020–8 December 2021) to provide insights into the economic benefits relative to the costs of vaccine development, manufacturing, and delivery.

Methods and findings

Public health outcomes of COVID-19 vaccination, including life years and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) gained from averted deaths, infections, and hospitalizations, were estimated. Health benefits were valued using two approaches: i) cost-benefit analysis and ii) cost-effectiveness analysis. title: A metabolomic signature of weight-loss and its associations with BMI-linked diseases: A post-hoc analysis of two intervention trials and a mendelian randomisation study
abstract:

Background

Obesity is a major risk factor for a broad spectrum of diseases, yet the molecular pathways underlying this risk remains poorly understood.
